name: Tanegashima Yoshinobu LP-1
tagline: Japan's heavy-lift gateway — H-IIA + H3, HTV / HTV-X cargo to the ISS
description: On Tanegashima, the southern Japanese island that's been home to JAXA's orbital programme since 1969. LP-1 hosted the H-II maiden flight in 1996; the H-IIA from 2001 (49 successes in 50 flights; retired June 2025 after its final mission); the seven HTV cargo flights to the ISS between 2009 and 2020; and from 2023 the new H3 rocket. Tanegashima's 30°N geometry is workable for geostationary launches — the south Pacific is empty downrange — and the fishing fleet stand-down windows are famously short, giving Japan some of the tightest launch-window protocols in the world.
best_known_for: Japan's heavy-lift gateway — H-IIA + H3, HTV / HTV-X cargo to the ISS
